name: Nathan Morris
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Culture Officer, Filevine (previously Chief of Strategic Partnerships)
profile: Nate Morris was a Las Vegas personal-injury litigator who co-founded Bighorn Law with Ryan Anderson. Frustrated by case-management tools, the two partnered with engineer Jim Blake in 2014 to build Filevine, now a Salt Lake City legal-software company that raised $400M in 2025 and sells AI tools to law firms.
interesting_fact: Filevine was born inside his own law firm: the founders' first goal was to get Bighorn Law 'off that Google spreadsheet' before selling the software to other firms.
deep_cut_fact: On the Capbase podcast he discussed how the Iron Man movies inspired Filevine's original MVP.

public_contacts.value: The Hoffman Agency for Filevine: filevine@hoffman.com

notes: Lower public profile than CEO Ryan Anderson; route via Filevine press. Titles vary across sources (CSP & CCO).

name: Jack Sharkey
profile: Self-taught developer and former teen sneaker botter who co-founded Whop in 2021 with Steven Schwartz and Cameron Zoub and built its Ruby on Rails platform. Whop, a marketplace for digital products, communities and courses, raised a $200M Series D at a $5.1B valuation in Oct 2026.
interesting_fact: Whop grew out of the teen sneaker-bot world: co-founders Schwartz and Zoub met building bots to buy limited-edition sneakers, and Sharkey joined as the third co-founder and engineer.
deep_cut_fact: His Rails World 2025 abstract: 'We started when Rails was "dead."' He says Whop processed $1B+ and handles 150k requests/minute on a single Rails monolith built by just 15 engineers.
notes: Developer-community persona (GitHub sharkey11). Hurun's $2B valuation is outdated ($5.1B Oct 2026).
